text: Seed multiplication plots need physical isolation from neighboring rice fields to prevent cross-mixing between varieties. The recommended layout, working inward from the field boundary: a 1.5-2 m buffer strip (ways of a different crop or a clear border) at the very edge, then a 0.5-1 m footpath/drainage strip, with the actual seed production plot in the center. Land preparation for the seed plot follows normal deep-ploughing practice - about 15-25 cm deep for clay-type soils and 8-12 cm for sandy soils, ploughed 2-3 times, then harrowed and leveled evenly so water drains and re-floods easily. For transplanting, seed multiplication plots use a wider, more open spacing than typical commercial paddy: rows spaced 20 cm × 20 cm, with only 1, or at most 2, seedlings per hill. This wider spacing and lower seedling count per hill is deliberate - it keeps individual plants easier to inspect during roguing (removing off-type plants), lowering the risk that impurities go unnoticed and end up mixed into the harvested seed lot.
